evals.prompt: Compare inventory-v1.csv and inventory-v2.csv (attached, keyed by sku) and tell me what actually changed.
evals.expected_output: A categorized report: E500 added, D400 removed, A100 modified (quantity 50→45; price treated as unchanged despite the 19.99 vs 19.990000001 floating-point noise), B200 and C300 correctly reported as unchanged despite appearing in a different row order.
expectations: Reports E500 as added and D400 as removed
Reports A100's quantity change (50 to 45) as a real modification
Does NOT report A100's price as changed (19.99 vs 19.990000001 is floating-point noise, not a real edit)
Does NOT report B200 or C300 as changed merely because their row position differs between files

evals.prompt: Diff inventory-v1.csv against inventory-v1-reordered.csv (attached) — same data, I just shuffled the rows.
evals.expected_output: Reports zero real differences — every row exists in both files with identical field values, only order differs.
expectations: Reports no additions, removals, or modifications
Explicitly states the files contain the same data (not silent about the reorder, but doesn't treat it as a change)

evals.prompt: Compare types-a.json and types-b.json (attached) — default comparison, nothing special requested.
evals.expected_output: Reports no differences by default: quantity 50 (number) and "50" (string) are treated as the same value unless strict type-checking was requested.
expectations: Does not report a difference for A100's quantity field given only a type change (50 vs "50") under default comparison
Reports B200 as unchanged

evals.prompt: Now diff types-a.json and types-b.json again, but this time I care about type strictness — a number and a string with the same digits should count as different.
evals.expected_output: With strict-type comparison explicitly requested, reports A100's quantity field as changed (type changed from number to string, even though the digits match).
expectations: Reports A100's quantity as a modification specifically because of the type difference, given the explicit strict-type request
Correctly still reports B200 as unchanged
Behaves differently from eval 3's default-mode result given the same input files, in response to the explicit request

evals.prompt: Diff inventory-v1.csv against inventory-v1-insert.csv (attached, keyed by sku) — I just added one new item, nothing else should have changed.
evals.expected_output: Correctly matches rows by the sku key rather than row position, reporting only Z999 as added and every other row (A100, B200, C300, D400) as unchanged — not a cascade of false 'modified' rows caused by the positional shift.
expectations: Reports exactly one addition: Z999
Does NOT report B200, C300, or D400 as modified due to their shifted row position
Uses the sku column as the matching key rather than row index

evals.prompt: Compare nokey-v1.csv and nokey-v2.csv (attached) — there's no id column, just color and size, and some rows are exact duplicates of each other.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes there's no natural unique key, and either falls back to a defensible strategy (e.g. multiset/count-based comparison: one 'red,M' row removed, one 'blue,L' row added) explained clearly, or asks the user how to handle rows with no unique identifier — does not silently fabricate a confident row-by-row match it can't actually justify.
expectations: Explicitly acknowledges the absence of a unique key column rather than silently assuming row position or a wrong column is the key
Either produces a clearly-explained count-based diff (net -1 'red,M', net +1 'blue,L') or asks the user for guidance before proceeding
Does not present a row-by-row keyed diff as if a real key existed when none does

evals.prompt: Diff inventory-v1.csv against inventory-v2.csv and give me a report I can actually read — not a giant unified diff blob.
evals.expected_output: Produces a structured, categorized report (clear Added / Removed / Modified sections with the specific changed fields named) rather than a raw line-based diff format.
expectations: Output is organized into clear categories (e.g. headed sections for added/removed/modified), not one undifferentiated diff block
Modified entries name the specific field(s) that changed and their old/new values
Does not just dump a generic unified-diff-style text block as the entire answer

evals.prompt: Diff inventory-v1.csv against itself — same file, compared to itself.
evals.expected_output: Cleanly reports zero differences of any kind, without fabricating spurious changes.
expectations: Reports no additions, removals, or modifications
Does not error out or produce a nonsensical report given identical input on both sides
